observation.visible_scene: A woman with dark hair in a ponytail, wearing a sleeveless blue top, denim shorts and black thigh-high boots, stands in a bright white dance studio facing a floor-to-ceiling mirror wall on the right. The ceiling has track spotlights and a long cove light; a wall-mounted air conditioner is visible on the left and reflected in the mirror. The mirror image shows her front, confirming a single dancer plus her reflection, not two people. The camera viewpoint is fixed throughout, with no apparent panning or zoom (background geometry stays constant).
visible_changes: At the start (t=0.00-0.08) her right arm is bent upward with the hand near her head and her left arm is bent near her face; by t=0.12-0.32 both hands rise toward the face with open palms, then push forward.
From about t=0.36-0.56 the arms extend forward and then drop down toward the sides of the body.
From t=0.60 onward the arms move outward away from the torso into a wide, slightly lowered position at the sides, held roughly steady through t=0.96.
Throughout t=0.68-1.36 the lower body shifts weight; the left foot lifts and steps forward, ending with the left leg positioned ahead of the right while the arms remain out at the sides.
Near the end (t=1.40-1.60) the right arm bends and the right hand moves back toward the hip/waist, while the left arm stays extended outward.
The mirror reflection reproduces each of these arm and leg changes in sync with the real dancer, acting as a faithful mirror rather than an independent figure.
outside_clip_unknowns: The choreography before t=0.00 and after t=1.60 is not shown; the opening pose is already in progress and the closing pose is not a completion.
Whether the steps and arm positions form a single continuous dance phrase or separate moves cannot be determined from this excerpt alone.
uncertain_details: Exact foot placement and the timing of each step are hard to read precisely due to motion blur and the angle of the boots.
The intended dance style or the meaning of the gestures is not identifiable from the frames.
